To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a cloned, hybridoma-cell line was established that secretes a monoclonal anti-glycolipid antibody, CAF-I, with specificity for a terminal disaccharidic epitope (glucuronic acid beta-1,4-galactose), and this epitope is expressed on the surface of imaginal discs and in the brain of the Drosophila larva, as well as the retinula cell elements of the Drosphila compound eye retina
the CAF-I antibody, raised against a terminal glucuronyl epitope of insect glycolipids, is a useful probe for the study of the glycolipid metabolism and the development of the insect nervous system.
the monoclonal anti-C. vicina glycolipids antibody CAF-I, recognizes a terminal disaccharidic epitope, glucuronic acid beta-1-4 galactose.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the epitope recognized by a cloned monoclonal antibody that is specific for a terminal glucurono-galactose epitope of insect glycolipids, and the distribution of this epitopes in the dipterous insect, Drosophala melanogaster.

the identification, characterization, and localization of a novel, insect-specific, terminal glucuronic-acid-containing epitope, and the production of a new monoclonal antibody that recognizes this epitope, which may be useful for the immunohistological identification of insect tissues.
the identification of a novel epitope of insect glycans, which is present in the glycolipids and glycoproteins of many species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epitope of monoclonal antibody CAI-I is the terminal disaccha-ride G1cA-beta-Ga1 beta-, and is expressed by most of the acidic glycolipid species in the dipterous insect, C. vicina.

the monoclonal anti-CAF-I antibody is a valuable tool to study the distribution of the terminal, nonreducing end of insect acidic glycosphingolipids in insect tissues, and to study the role of the CAF-I epitopes in the development of insects.
CAF-I recognizes an epitope of the terminal glucuronic residue of acidic glycolipid molecules in the insect, C. vicina.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CAF-I monoclonal antibody recognizes a terminal glucuronyl residue of acidic glycolipid, which is expressed in a specific developmental pattern in the Drosophila imaginal discs and the retina.
the monoclonal CAF-I antibody recognizes a terminal glucuronyl epitope of insect glycolipids and is useful as a probe for the study of glycolipid distribution during insect development.

the monoclonal anti-CAF-I antibody recognizes an oligosaccharidic epitope of a group of acidic glycolipid molecules, which have the common structural feature of a terminal non-reducing glucuronic acid residue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CAF-I epitopes of acidic glycolipid are widely distributed among insect taxa, and are present in a variety of tissues, including the nervous system.
the CAF-I monoclonal antibody can be used as an immunohistological marker of the imaginal discs of D. melanogaster, and the ommatidia of the compound eyes of adult females.
the CAF-I monoclonal antibody can be a valuable tool in the analysis of the glycolipids in the tissues of insects and other invertebrate species.
